name: The dialectic (thesis, antithesis, synthesis)
plain_explanation: Hegel's method for showing that any single idea about reality, followed through carefully, turns out to be incomplete or self-contradictory (the 'thesis'), forcing us to an opposite idea (the 'antithesis') that is equally incomplete, until both are combined and corrected in a fuller idea (the 'synthesis') -- a process Hegel thought could be repeated until we reach the fullest possible conception of reality, the 'Absolute Idea.'
precise_definition: Hegel's triadic logical-metaphysical method, by which any predicate taken to characterize Reality as a whole is shown to be self-contradictory (thesis), driving thought to an opposite predicate that is equally self-contradictory (antithesis), and thence to a synthesis that incorporates and corrects both, with each synthesis becoming the thesis of a new triad, until the process culminates in the Absolute Idea.
why_it_mattered: It is Hegel's proposed method for deducing the nature of reality by pure logic alone, and it structures both his Logic (Being -> Nothing -> Becoming, etc.) and his Philosophy of History, where Russell argues (without full justification from Hegel's own metaphysics) that world history is claimed to literally repeat the transitions of the dialectic.
historical_origin: Hegel's Science of Logic and Encyclopaedia Logic.
examples: Russell's 'uncle' illustration: 'Reality is an uncle' (thesis) implies a nephew, so 'The Absolute is a nephew' (antithesis), synthesized into the whole composed of uncle-and-nephew, which itself proves incomplete and must be further enlarged
Hegel's own opening move: 'The Absolute is Pure Being' (thesis) -> 'The Absolute is Nothing' (antithesis) -> 'The Absolute is Becoming' (synthesis)
objections: Russell argues the underlying logical assumption -- that relations cannot be real because traditional subject-predicate logic can only handle a single thing having a single quality -- is simply mistaken, and that this mistake, not genuine insight, generates the 'imposing edifice' of Hegel's system.

Russell notes there is no justification, even within Hegel's own metaphysic, for supposing that the time-process of world history must repeat the purely logical transitions of the dialectic, since on Hegel's view time itself is not fully real.
competing_positions: Modern relational/analytic logic, which allows genuine relations between distinct things without requiring reduction to statements about a single Whole
influence_on_later_thinkers: Directly inherited (with a materialist inversion) by Marx as dialectical materialism.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Applied by Hegel to world history, where it becomes the engine of his account of nations and Spirit's progress toward freedom.
